title: Morristown Medical Center: #1 for Cardiac Care in NJ
text: Morristown Medical Centre Leads New Jersey in Cardiac Care, New Rankings Show New data reveals Morristown Medical Center performed the highest number of cardiac procedures in New Jersey in 2023, solidifying its position as a leading provider of heart care in the state. The rankings, compiled by the NJBIZ Leads & Data Center, highlight the significant contributions of hospitals across the Garden State to cardiovascular health. Did you know? – morristown Medical Center led the state with 6,906 cardiac procedures in 2023. This included 1,360 open heart surgeries and 1,883 PCI procedures. The hospitalS volume underscores its commitment to complete heart care. Leading the State in Cardiac Procedures Morristown medical Center handled an remarkable 6,906 cardiac procedures throughout 2023. This included 1,360 open heart surgeries and 1,883 total Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) procedures – a minimally invasive treatment to open blocked coronary arteries. Pro tip: – PCI procedures, a minimally invasive option, are used to open blocked coronary arteries. Morristown Medical Center performed 1,883 such procedures in 2023. This highlights the hospital’s focus on advanced cardiac treatments. Hackensack Meridian Jersey Shore University Medical center followed closely in second place, completing 5,868 cardiac services. Surgeons at the Neptune facility performed 780 open heart operations and treated 1,729 patients with PCI procedures. Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital in New Brunswick secured the third spot, processing 3,880 cardiac cases and performing 735 open heart surgeries. Rounding out the top five were Hackensack University Medical Center in Hackensack, with 3,609 procedures, and AtlantiCare Regional Medical Center’s Mainland campus in Pomona, with 3,560 procedures. These facilities completed 744 and 255 open heart surgeries,respectively. Reader question: – How do these rankings impact patient care? The data helps patients understand hospital performance. It also highlights the diverse approaches to cardiac care across New Jersey hospitals, offering insights into treatment options. Specialized Care and Evolving Landscape The data also reveals a diverse range of cardiac care approaches across New Jersey hospitals. Notably, several facilities focused on non-surgical interventions. Hackensack Meridian JFK University Medical Center completed 3,348 cardiac services without performing any open heart operations, while RWJBarnabas Health Community Medical Center handled 1,911 procedures, also without heart surgery. the healthcare landscape in New Jersey is also undergoing changes. Cooper University Health Care merged with Cape Regional Health System during 2024, and Atlantic Health System planned a partnership with Saint Peter’s Healthcare System .Though, these developments occurred after the data collection period for the 2023 rankings. data Collection and Methodology The NJBIZ rankings are based on statistics compiled by the New Jersey Department of Health from January through December 2023, supplemented by research conducted by NJBIZ. The data encompasses a broad spectrum of cardiac care, including diagnostic tests, elective interventions, and emergency treatments . Each participating facility submitted data detailing its contributions to cardiac care throughout the state. Comcast Business and Provident Bank are Premium Publication Sponsors of NJBIZ’s 2025 Book of Lists, and Hackensack Meridian Health serves as the Chapter Sponsor of the Health Care & Pharmaceuticals chapter.
